en.name: Jams, jellies and preserves
en.summary: Jams, jellies and preserves are fruit set with sugar and acid, which is a preservation system in its own right. Unopened they keep about 6–18 months from purchase in the cupboard. Once opened they go in the fridge, where about 6–12 months is the range.
en.pantry: An unopened jar keeps about 6–18 months from purchase, cool, dark and dry. The wide range reflects a wide family: a high-sugar traditional jam sits at the long end, and a reduced-sugar or no-added-sugar product at the short end, because the sugar is not decoration but the thing doing the preserving. Store jars upright, out of sunlight, and discard any whose lid has lost its vacuum. Home-canned jars belong here too, dated and used oldest first.
en.fridge: Once opened, keep it at 4 °C (40 °F) or below and use within about 6–12 months. The single habit that decides whether a jar reaches that is the spoon: crumbs, butter and a knife that has been across toast are how a sugary, otherwise stable preserve grows mould. Keep a clean spoon for the jar, wipe the rim before closing, and do not leave it on the breakfast table all morning. Reduced-sugar jams sit at the short end of the range.
en.freezer: There is no freezer timeline for jams and preserves in the jar, and there is little reason to freeze a food that already keeps for months. Freezer jam is a different product — an uncooked, lightly set fruit spread deliberately made to be stored frozen and kept in the fridge once thawed — and it follows the recipe it was made to, not this entry. For an ordinary jar, cupboard and fridge have it covered.
spoilage: Mould spots on the surface or under the lid — discard the whole jar, not just the spot
A fermented, yeasty or alcoholic smell, or fizzing on opening
A lid that has domed up, or a jar that spurts when opened
Liquid weeping out with a darkened, dull colour
tips: Keep one clean spoon for the jar and never use a knife that has been on toast.
Wipe the rim before closing so the lid seats properly.
Write the opening date on the lid and work through jars oldest first.
Treat reduced-sugar jams as the perishable end — less sugar means less preservation.

faq.q: Does jam need to be refrigerated after opening?
faq.a: Yes. Keep it at 4 °C or below and use within about 6–12 months.

faq.q: How long does unopened jam last?
faq.a: About 6–18 months from purchase in a cool dark cupboard. Reduced-sugar jams sit at the shorter end.

faq.q: Can you scrape mould off jam and eat the rest?
faq.a: No. A soft, moist preserve is colonised beyond the visible spot. Discard the jar.
There is no timeline and little need — it already keeps for months. Freezer jam is a separate recipe made specifically for the freezer.

zh.name: 果醬與果凍醬
zh.summary: 果醬、果凍醬和蜜餞醬是用糖和酸把水果凝結起來，這本身就是一套保存機制。未開封放櫥櫃，從購買日起算大約 6～18 個月。開封後要進冰箱，大約 6～12 個月。
zh.pantry: 未開封的罐子從購買日起算大約 6～18 個月，放在陰涼、避光、乾燥處。範圍這麼寬是因為這一家族本來就很廣：傳統高糖果醬落在長的那端，減糖或無添加糖的產品落在短的那端，因為糖不是裝飾，它就是在做保存工作的那個東西。請直立擺放、避免日曬，蓋子已經沒有真空感的就丟掉。自製封罐的果醬也放這裡，標好日期、先做先用。
zh.fridge: 開封後請放 4 °C 以下，並在大約 6～12 個月內用完。決定一罐能不能撐到那個期限的，就是湯匙這件事：麵包屑、奶油，還有剛抹過吐司的刀，正是讓一罐高糖、本來很穩定的果醬長霉的原因。請為它準備一支專用的乾淨湯匙，蓋回去前擦瓶口，也不要讓它在早餐桌上擺一整個上午。減糖果醬請算在範圍裡較短的那一端。
zh.freezer: 罐裝果醬沒有冷凍期限，而且一個本來就能放好幾個月的食物，也沒什麼冷凍的必要。「冷凍果醬」是另一種產品——未經熬煮、凝結很輕、本來就設計成冷凍保存、解凍後放冷藏的果醬抹——它依照自己的配方走，不適用這一篇。一般罐裝果醬，櫥櫃加冰箱就夠了。
spoilage: 醬面或蓋子內側出現霉點——整罐丟掉，不是只挖掉那一塊
有發酵味、酵母味或酒味，或開罐時冒氣
蓋子鼓起，或開罐時噴出
滲出液體、顏色變深變暗
tips: 為果醬準備一支專用乾淨湯匙，絕不用抹過吐司的刀。
蓋回去前擦瓶口，蓋子才能確實密合。
在蓋子上寫開封日期，並先開先用。
減糖果醬要當成易腐的那一端——糖少，保存力就少。

faq.a: 要。放 4 °C 以下，並在大約 6～12 個月內用完。

faq.q: 未開封的果醬可以放多久？
faq.a: 陰涼避光的櫥櫃，從購買日起算大約 6～18 個月。減糖款屬於較短的那一端。

faq.q: 果醬長霉可以挖掉繼續吃嗎？
faq.a: 不行。柔軟含水的果醬，霉早已經超出看得見的範圍。整罐丟掉。
沒有對應期限，也沒什麼必要——它本來就能放好幾個月。「冷凍果醬」是專為冷凍設計的另一種配方。
